newsitem.title: UK: Strong sterling drives UK wheat futures down.
newsitem.headline: Strong sterling drives UK wheat futures down.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures closed lower as sterling's strength again set the tone, traders said.
One described wheat's erratic downward path as "a bit of a yo-yo."
There was some shipper buying in the morning, and some consumer buying later to help limit falls, he said.

But neither factor was enough to stop all but one of the wheat contracts ending at the day's lows. The exception was May, the most active month, which last traded 0.85 stg lower at 95.70 stg, compared to a low of 95.60. March volume was 191 lots.
Total wheat volume was 340 lots, which one trader described as "not too bad."
Barley futures were compeletely neglected, with no trade whatsoever.

The friendly effect of Thursday's EU grains tender had worn off quickly, traders said. UK interest had been especially high, as the imminence of a likely green rate revaluation made getting a licence this week a potentially more attractive proposition than licences issued after a change.
The revaluation, likely on January 21, would cut the sterling value of EU export refunds.
